findings.finding: B2B SaaS ventures with CAC/LTV ratio below 0.15 demonstrate 2x faster growth and higher customer retention than those with ratios above 0.5
findings.statistical_note: Observed across 3 ventures with sufficient scale (>150 customers or >$40K MRR). Effect size ranges from 18% to 22% monthly growth for low-ratio ventures vs 5% for high-ratio ventures.
findings.actionable_implication: Prioritize unit economics validation early in venture lifecycle. Ventures with strong CAC/LTV ratios (<0.15) should pursue aggressive scaling; those with ratios >0.5 require fundamental business model rethinking before scaling.

findings.finding: Ventures entering regulated markets (healthcare, finance) experience 4-6 month longer sales cycles than unrestricted SaaS, increasing required runway 40-60%
findings.statistical_note: Healthcare cycle observed at 20 weeks vs 8 weeks baseline. Sample size of 1 venture; confidence would increase with additional healthcare ventures.
findings.actionable_implication: For regulated verticals, model 6-month sales cycles minimum and plan runway accordingly. Enterprise sales hiring and compliance investment should occur earlier than for unrestricted SaaS.

findings.finding: Supply chain and logistics software ventures without founding team domain expertise show <5% conversion rates despite industry benchmarks of 8-12%, correlating with high CAC/LTV ratios (0.75+)
findings.statistical_note: Single venture with detailed postmortem data. Pattern supported by cross-enterprise sales dynamics in logistics vertical showing high switching costs and entrenched incumbents.
findings.actionable_implication: Require domain expertise validation (customer advisory board, founder background) before structuring supply chain ventures. Alternatively, acquire domain expertise through hires before GTM launch.

correlations.caveat: Correlation observed among B2B SaaS ventures only; relationship may not hold for other business models. Growth sustainability also depends on churn and retention.
Supply chain domain expertise correlated with faster sales cycle, but sample limited to 1 venture. Market access and buyer relationships likely confounders.
Freemium model (DataFlow) showed low CAC but free-to-paid conversion required sales team. Enterprise direct sales (MediLink) had high CAC but higher LTV. Not a simple comparison.

counter_intuitive_findings.finding: Longer sales cycles did not prevent traction in healthcare SaaS; MediLink achieved $120K ARR in 18 weeks despite 20-week sales cycles
counter_intuitive_findings.why_surprising: Conventional wisdom suggests long sales cycles kill velocity. However, high enterprise contract values and strong product-market fit in healthcare allowed MediLink to grow despite procurement delays.
